10.29.7.b.d: तां सर्वे ऽध्वर्यवो ऽग्रेण प्राग्वंशं राजन्योह्यमान उद्गृह्णन्ति
10.29.7.b.m: all the adhvaryus lift it up in front of the prāgvaṃśa hall while the King is being conveyed.

10.29.9.a.s: agreṇa prāgvaṃśaṃ prāgīṣamudagīṣaṃ vā śakaṭamavasthāpya pūrvvadākhidyopastabhya varuṇasya skambhanamasīti śamyāmudvṛhya vicṛtto varuṇasya pāśa iti yoktrapāśaṃ vicṛtyonmukto varuṇasya pāśa ityabhidhānīmunmuñcati
10.29.9.a.d: अग्रेण प्राग्वंशं प्रागीषमुदगीषं वा शकटमवस्थाप्य पूर्व्वदाखिद्योपस्तभ्य वरुणस्य स्कम्भनमसीति शम्यामुद्वृह्य विचृत्तो वरुणस्य पाश इति योक्त्रपाशं विचृत्योन्मुक्तो वरुणस्य पाश इत्यभिधानीमुन्मुञ्चति
10.29.9.a.m: Having halted the cart in front of the prāgvaṃśa hall, with its shafts facing east or facing north, having pulled it down and propped it up as before, having taken off the yoke-peg with 'You are the prop of Varuṇa,' having untied the yoke-strap loop with 'Untied is the bond of Varuṇa,' he removes the halter with 'Loosed is the bond of Varuṇa.'

10.29.10.a.m: In the same manner, he unyokes the northern ox.

10.29.11.a.m: The left [ox] is either unyoked or not unyoked.

10.30.1.a.m: Then he undertakes the procedure of the guest-offering (ātithyā).

10.30.2.a.m: The firewood consists of twenty-two sticks.

10.30.3.c.m: the enclosing sticks are made of kārṣmarya wood.

10.30.3.d.m: Having made the grass broom (veda) and strewn around the fires, he undertakes the ritual acts beginning with the washing of the hands.

10.30.4.a.m: The placement of the utensils is according to requirement.

10.30.5.a.m: At the time of portioning out the oblation, having made the sacrificer's wife hold onto the cart, he portions out the guest-offering;

10.30.7.b.m: Portioning out from the hand, he should mutter all the cart mantras over the hand,

10.30.8.a.m: formula by formula, beginning with 'You are the hospitality for Agni...'

10.30.9.a.m: There is a substitute mention of the deity.

10.30.10.a.m: In the case of the five [portions], he appends the formula dedicated to Savitṛ and 'agreeable to...'

10.30.12.a.m: The sacrificial cake is dedicated to Viṣṇu, on nine potsherds.

10.30.13.a.m: From here onwards, the preparatory rites are just as for Viṣṇu.

10.30.14.a.m: Having released speech with the invocation of the preparer of the oblation (haviṣkṛt), and having unyoked the northern ox,

10.30.15.a.s: vāruṇamasīti vāso 'pādāya varuṇo 'si dhṛtavrata iti rājānamādāyācchidrapatraḥ prajā upāvarohośannuśatīḥ syonaḥ syonāḥ soma rānviśvastvaṃ prajā upāvaroha viśvāstvāṃ prajā upāvarohantvityupāvahṛtyorvantarikṣamanvihīty abhipravrajati
10.30.15.a.d: वारुणमसीति वासो ऽपादाय वरुणो ऽसि धृतव्रत इति राजानमादायाच्छिद्रपत्रः प्रजा उपावरोहोशन्नुशतीः स्योनः स्योनाः सोम रान्विश्वस्त्वं प्रजा उपावरोह विश्वास्त्वां प्रजा उपावरोहन्त्वित्युपावहृत्योर्वन्तरिक्षमन्विहीत्य् अभिप्रव्रजति
10.30.15.a.m: having taken off the cloth with 'You belong to Varuṇa,' having taken the King with 'You are Varuṇa whose vows are steadfast,' having taken him down with 'With unperforated leaf, descend to the offspring; desiring [them who are] desiring, kind [to them who are] kind; O King Soma, descend to all offspring, may all offspring descend to you,' he steps forward with 'Traverse the wide atmosphere.'

10.31.1.a.m: Taking the chair, the pratiprasthātṛ proceeds in front.

10.31.2.a.s: yā te dhāmānīti pūrvayā dvārā prāgvaṃśaṃ praviśyāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātihṛtya varuṇasyartasadanyasīti dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ rājāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
10.31.2.a.d: या ते धामानीति पूर्वया द्वारा प्राग्वंशं प्रविश्यापरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिहृत्य वरुणस्यर्तसदन्यसीति दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं राजासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठापयति
10.31.2.a.m: Having entered the prāgvaṃśa hall through the eastern door with 'Whatever your abodes...', having carried it past southwards to the west of the āhavanīya, he sets down the King's chair south of the āhavanīya with 'You are the seat of the cosmic order belonging to Varuṇa.'

10.31.3.a.m: Upon it, the spreading of the black antelope skin and the placing of the King take place as on the cart.

10.31.4.a.d: वरुणो ऽसि धृतव्रत इति राजानम् अभिमन्त्रयते
10.31.4.a.m: He addresses the King with 'You are Varuṇa whose vows are steadfast.'

10.31.5.a.m: With 'You belong to Varuṇa,' he wraps him around with a cloth.

10.31.6.a.s: evāvandasva varuṇaṃ bṛhantaṃ namasyā dhīramamṛtasya gopām /
10.31.6.a.d: एवावन्दस्व वरुणं बृहन्तं नमस्या धीरममृतस्य गोपाम् ।
10.31.6.a.m: He should seat the King in all cases with this verse: 'Thus praise great Varuṇa; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality;

10.31.6.b.s: sa naḥ śarma trivarūthaṃ viyaṃsatpātaṃ mā dyāvāpṛthivī upastha ity etayā sarvatra rājānamāsīdet
10.31.6.b.d: स नः शर्म त्रिवरूथं वियंसत्पातं मा द्यावापृथिवी उपस्थ इत्य् एतया सर्वत्र राजानमासीदेत्
10.31.6.b.m: may he extend three-layered protection to us; do you protect me in your lap, O Heaven and Earth.'

10.31.7.a.s: agniṃ rājānaṃ cāntareṇa mā saṃcāriṣṭeti saṃpreṣyati
10.31.7.a.d: अग्निं राजानं चान्तरेण मा संचारिष्टेति संप्रेष्यति
10.31.7.a.m: He issues the call: 'Do not pass between the fire and the king!'

10.31.8.a.m: He undertakes the rites beginning with pounding [the grains].

10.31.10.a.m: Having deposited the ātithya [offering] with the Caturhotṛ formula, he recites the saṃbhārayajus formulas.

10.31.11.a.m: Some [authorities] say that he makes the sacrificer recite [them].

10.31.12.a.m: The churning [of fire] and the sāmidhenī verses are [performed] like those of an animal sacrifice.

10.31.14.a.m: At the fourth, he empties the entire contents of the upabhṛt [into the juhū].

10.31.16.a.m: He preserves the clarified butter from the dhruvā spoon.

11.1.1.a.s: ātithyāyā dhrauvātsruci camase vā tānūnaptraṃ samavadyati /
11.1.1.a.d: आतिथ्याया ध्रौवात्स्रुचि चमसे वा तानूनप्त्रं समवद्यति ।
11.1.1.a.m: From the dhruvā of the ātithya, he cuts off the portions for the tānūnaptra into a ladling spoon or into a goblet

11.1.1.b.m: in four portions or in five portions

11.1.1.c.m: with the formulas, 'For Āpati I take you...', one after each formula.

11.1.2.a.m: With 'You are unassailable...', the priests, seventeen including the sacrificer, touch the tānūnaptra together.

11.1.3.a.m: The sacrificer says, 'According to my consecration...'

11.1.4.a.m: Whomever he wishes, 'May he attain fame in sacrifice', him [he should make touch it] first;

11.1.4.b.m: if he should desire for all [to attain it], he should make them all touch it at the same time.

11.1.5.a.m: It is said [in the brāhmaṇa]: 'Therefore, whichever [breach arises] among those who have partaken of the tānūnaptra...'

11.1.6.a.s: prajāpatau tvā manasi juhomīti yajamānastānūnaptraṃ triravajighrati
11.1.6.a.d: प्रजापतौ त्वा मनसि जुहोमीति यजमानस्तानूनप्त्रं त्रिरवजिघ्रति
11.1.6.a.m: With 'In Prajāpati, in the mind, I offer you', the sacrificer smells the tānūnaptra three times.

11.1.7.a.m: Or on following days he pours [it] into his fast-milk.

11.1.8.a.m: He asks: 'Agnīdh, are the waters boiling?'

11.1.9.a.s: madanti devīramṛtā ṛtāvṛdha ity āgnīdhraḥ pratyāha
11.1.9.a.d: मदन्ति देवीरमृता ऋतावृध इत्य् आग्नीध्रः प्रत्याह
11.1.9.a.m: The āgnīdhra replies: 'They are boiling, the divine, immortal enhancers of cosmic order.'

11.1.10.a.m: He gives the call: 'Come with them.'

11.1.11.a.s: madantīrupaspṛśya tānūnaptriṇo visrasya rājānaṃ sahiraṇyaiḥ pāṇibhirāpyāyayantyaṃśuraṃśuste deva somāpyāyatāmiti
11.1.11.a.d: मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य तानूनप्त्रिणो विस्रस्य राजानं सहिरण्यैः पाणिभिराप्याययन्त्यंशुरंशुस्ते देव सोमाप्यायतामिति
11.1.11.a.m: Having touched the boiling waters, untied the tānūnaptra, they swell the king [Soma] with hands holding gold, [reciting,] 'May stalk by stalk swell for you, divine Soma...'

11.1.12.b.s: dakṣiṇe vedyante prastaraṃ nidhāya dakṣiṇānpāṇīnuttānānkṛtvā savyānnīca eṣṭā rāyaḥ preṣe bhagāyeti
11.1.12.b.d: दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते प्रस्तरं निधाय दक्षिणान्पाणीनुत्तानान्कृत्वा सव्यान्नीच एष्टा रायः प्रेषे भगायेति
11.1.12.b.m: having placed the grass bunch at the southern edge of the altar ground and turned their right hands palms upward and left hands downwards, with 'Desirous of wealth, for impulse, for fortune...'

11.1.13.a.m: Then the sacrificer enters upon the intermediate consecration.

11.1.14.a.m: He attends upon the āhavanīya fire with 'O Agni, lord of vows, you are the lord of vows of vows.'

11.1.15.a.m: According to the Vājasaneyaka, with this very formula he puts a kindling stick on it.

11.2.3.a.m: He wipes himself with boiling water.

11.2.4.a.s: yā te agne rudriyā tanūrityetenaivāta ūrdhvaṃ vratayati
11.2.4.a.d: या ते अग्ने रुद्रिया तनूरित्येतेनैवात ऊर्ध्वं व्रतयति
11.2.4.a.m: From this point onward, he drinks the fast-food only with 'That body of yours, Agni, which is fierce...'

11.2.5.a.m: Having performed the Pravargya, they proceed with the Upasad,

11.2.6.a.m: He should not perform the Pravargya at a first sacrifice;

11.2.8.a.m: he may perform it for a bad Brahmin;

11.2.9.a.m: some say, for one who desires spiritual lustre;

11.2.10.a.m: The Bahvṛca Brāhmaṇa says: 'For one who is learned and proficient in the Vedas, he should perform the Pravargya.'

11.2.11.a.m: The sacrificial grass of the ātithya serves for the Upasads and for the Agnīṣomīya [rite];

11.2.11.b.m: and the same serves for the grass bunch and the enclosing sticks.

11.2.12.a.m: Some say: that sacrificial grass remains strewn, those enclosing sticks remain set around.

11.2.13.a.m: He commences the procedure of the Upasad.

11.2.14.a.m: The firewood is the normal one, or consists of ten sticks.

11.2.15.a.m: Having made the veda, having strewn around the fires, he undertakes the rites beginning with washing the hands

11.2.15.b.m: He arranges the utensils according to purpose.

11.2.16.a.s: sphyamagnihotrahavaṇīṃ sruvaṃ juhūmupabhṛtaṃ dhruvāṃ vedamājyasthālīmiti dvandvaṇ prayujya pavitre kṛtvā yajamāna vācaṃ yaccheti saṃpreṣyati
11.2.16.a.d: स्फ्यमग्निहोत्रहवणीं स्रुवं जुहूमुपभृतं ध्रुवां वेदमाज्यस्थालीमिति द्वन्द्वण् प्रयुज्य पवित्रे कृत्वा यजमान वाचं यच्छेति संप्रेष्यति
11.2.16.a.m: Having arranged in pairs the wooden sword, the agnihotra ladle, the sruva spoon, the juhū, the upabhṛt, the dhruvā, the veda, and the clarified butter pot, and having prepared the strainers, he calls: 'Sacrificer, restrain your speech!'

11.2.17.a.s: vāgyataḥ pātrāṇi saṃmṛśya prokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtya brahmāṇamāmantrya pātrāṇi prokṣati
11.2.17.a.d: वाग्यतः पात्राणि संमृश्य प्रोक्षणीः संस्कृत्य ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य पात्राणि प्रोक्षति
11.2.17.a.m: Restraining speech, having touched the utensils, purified the sprinkling waters, and addressed the brahman, he sprinkles the utensils.

11.3.1.a.s: lomabhyo 'dhi stambayajurhṛtvottaraṃ parigrāhaṃ parigṛhya saṃpreṣyati prokṣaṇīrāsādayedhmamupasādaya sruvaṃ ca srucaśca saṃmṛḍḍhyājyenodehīti
11.3.1.a.d: लोमभ्यो ऽधि स्तम्बयजुर्हृत्वोत्तरं परिग्राहं परिगृह्य संप्रेष्यति प्रोक्षणीरासादयेध्ममुपसादय स्रुवं च स्रुचश्च संमृड्ढ्याज्येनोदेहीति
11.3.1.a.m: and taking away the stambayajus from the hair-points [of the ground], having outlined the northern second tracing, he issues the call: 'Set down the sprinkling waters, set near the firewood, wipe clean the sruva and the sruc spoons, and come up with clarified butter!'

11.3.2.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, he takes it only into the dhruvā.

11.3.2.b.s: prokṣaṇīrabhimantrya brahmāṇamāmantryedhmaṃ vediṃ ca prokṣya prokṣaṇīśeṣaṃ ninīya pavitre apisṛjyaikāmāghārasamidhamādhāyāntarvedi vidhṛtī nidhāya dhruvāṃ sruvaṃ ca sādayati etāvasadatāmiti mantraṃ saṃnamati
11.3.2.b.d: प्रोक्षणीरभिमन्त्र्य ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्येध्मं वेदिं च प्रोक्ष्य प्रोक्षणीशेषं निनीय पवित्रे अपिसृज्यैकामाघारसमिधमाधायान्तर्वेदि विधृती निधाय ध्रुवां स्रुवं च सादयति एतावसदतामिति मन्त्रं संनमति
11.3.2.b.m: Having consecrated the sprinkling waters, addressed the brahman, sprinkled the firewood and the altar ground, poured down the remainder of the sprinkling waters, discarded the strainers, placed one kindling stick for the āghāra libation, and placed the two separating blades inside the altar ground, he sets down the dhruvā and the sruva; he adapts the formula: 'May these two sit down...'

11.3.3.a.m: Having laid down the veda, he proceeds to the sāmidhenī verses.

11.3.6.a.m: He should offer no other oblation before [these].

11.3.8.a.m: He chooses neither the ancestral lineage (ārṣeya) nor the hotṛ.

11.3.8.b.m: Having called for the response, he says, 'Be seated, O hotṛ.'

11.3.9.a.m: From the dhruvā ladling, he takes eight [portions of clarified butter] into the juhū,

11.3.10.a.s: ghṛtavati śabde juhūpabhṛtāvādāya dakṣiṇā sakṛdatikrānta upāṃśuyājavatpracarati
11.3.10.a.d: घृतवति शब्दे जुहूपभृतावादाय दक्षिणा सकृदतिक्रान्त उपांशुयाजवत्प्रचरति
11.3.10.a.m: At the word 'possessing clarified butter' (ghṛtavatī), having taken up the juhū and upabhṛt, having stepped across southwards once, he proceeds in the manner of the low-voice offering (upāṃśuyāja).

11.3.11.a.m: With half of the [butter] in the juhū, he sacrifices to Agni;

11.3.12.a.s: aupabhṛtaṃ juhvāmānīya viṣṇumiṣṭvā pratyākramya yā te agne 'yāśayā tanūriti sruveṇopasadaṃ juhoti
11.3.12.a.d: औपभृतं जुह्वामानीय विष्णुमिष्ट्वा प्रत्याक्रम्य या ते अग्ने ऽयाशया तनूरिति स्रुवेणोपसदं जुहोति
11.3.12.a.m: Having poured the [butter] from the upabhṛt into the juhū and sacrificed to Viṣṇu, having stepped back, he offers the Upasad with the sruva with the mantra: 'O Agni, that body of yours resting in iron...'

11.3.13.a.m: Having performed the reverences beginning with 'Do the waters rejoice, O Agni...', [he issues the call:] 'Agnīdh, announce the wives of the gods! Subrahmaṇya, call the Subrahmaṇyā!'

11.3.14.a.s: apareṇa gārhapatyamāgnīdhra upaviśya devapatnīrvyācaṣṭe senendrasya dheneti /
11.3.14.a.d: अपरेण गार्हपत्यमाग्नीध्र उपविश्य देवपत्नीर्व्याचष्टे सेनेन्द्रस्य धेनेति ।
11.3.14.a.m: Having sat down to the west of the gārhapatya, the āgnīdhra announces the wives of the gods [with the formula]: 'Indra's wife, the milch cow...'

11.3.14.b.m: [The subrahmaṇya] calls the Subrahmaṇyā on the rubbish heap (utkara).

11.3.14.c.m: As before, the sacrificer follows it with mantras.

11.4.1.a.m: Early in the morning, they perform the morning Pravargya and Upasads;

11.4.1.b.m: late in the afternoon, the afternoon ones.

11.4.2.a.m: In the evening, however, the reverence is performed with left palms turned upward.

11.4.4.a.m: In this manner is the performance with the latter two.

11.4.5.a.m: He offers with 'resting in silver' at the second;

11.4.6.a.m: The matter of which are the morning consecratory verses has [already] been stated.

11.4.7.a.m: There are only three Upasads for a one-day sacrifice;

11.4.8.a.s: yadi saṃgrāmaṃ puro vā yudhyeyur ayaḥ prathamāyāyāmavadhāya juhuyāt /
11.4.8.a.d: यदि संग्रामं पुरो वा युध्येयुर् अयः प्रथमायायामवधाय जुहुयात् ।
11.4.8.a.m: If they should fight a battle in front, he should make the offering having inserted iron in the first [Upasad];

11.4.9.a.m: The regulation of the teats is 'pointed like an awl'.

11.4.10.a.m: On the day they buy Soma, they should milk four [teats] in the evening, three in the morning, two in the evening, and one on the last [day];

11.4.11.a.m: Between the middle Pravargya and Upasad, they prepare the altar ground.

11.4.12.a.m: Having stepped three steps eastwards from the middle roof-pin (lalāṭikā) of the eastern hall, he drives in a peg.

11.4.13.a.m: From that [peg], at fifteen [steps] to the south [he drives a peg];

11.4.13.d.m: Thirty-six [steps] to the east of the first-driven peg [he drives a peg];

11.4.13.e.m: from that, at twelve [steps] to the south [he drives a peg];

11.4.14.a.s: vimime tvā payasvatīṃ devānāṃ dhenuṃ sudughāmanapasphurantīm /
11.4.14.a.d: विमिमे त्वा पयस्वतीं देवानां धेनुं सुदुघामनपस्फुरन्तीम् ।
11.4.14.a.m: 'I measure you out, the full-of-milk cow of the gods, easily milked, not kicking away;

11.4.14.b.s: indraḥ somaṃ pibatu kṣemo astu na iti vimānaḥ
11.4.14.b.d: इन्द्रः सोमं पिबतु क्षेमो अस्तु न इति विमानः
11.4.14.b.m: May Indra drink soma, may safety be ours,' [reciting this,] he measures [the altar ground].

11.4.15.a.m: He stretches [the cord] all around with a measuring line (spandyā);

11.5.1.a.s: imāṃ naraḥ kṛṇuta vedimetya vasumatīṃ rudravatīmādityavatīṃ varṣmandivo nābhā pṛthivyā yathāyaṃ yajamāno na riṣyeddevasya savituḥ sava iti saṃpreṣyati
11.5.1.a.d: इमां नरः कृणुत वेदिमेत्य वसुमतीं रुद्रवतीमादित्यवतीं वर्ष्मन्दिवो नाभा पृथिव्या यथायं यजमानो न रिष्येद्देवस्य सवितुः सव इति संप्रेष्यति
11.5.1.a.m: He issues the call: 'O men, having approached, make this altar ground accompanied by the Vasus, accompanied by the Rudras, accompanied by the Ādityas, on the highest point of heaven, at the navel of the earth, so that this sacrificer will not be harmed, at the impulse of the god Savitṛ!'

11.5.2.a.s: sphyena vighanena parśvā paraśunā ca vediṃ kurvanti
11.5.2.a.d: स्फ्येन विघनेन पर्श्वा परशुना च वेदिं कुर्वन्ति
11.5.2.a.m: With the wooden sword (sphya), with the mallet, with the rib, and with the axe, they prepare the altar ground.

11.5.3.a.s: darśapūrṇamāsavatsaṃnamanavarjaṃ prāguttarātparigrāhātkṛtvā catuḥśikhaṇḍā yuvatiḥ supeśā ghṛtapratīkā bhuvanasya madhye /
11.5.3.a.d: दर्शपूर्णमासवत्संनमनवर्जं प्रागुत्तरात्परिग्राहात्कृत्वा चतुःशिखण्डा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका भुवनस्य मध्ये ।
11.5.3.a.m: Having performed [the work] as in the New and Full Moon sacrifices, omitting the bending down, prior to the northern tracing, [and having touched the altar ground] with: 'Having four locks of hair, youthful, well-adorned, ghee-faced, in the middle of the world;

11.5.3.b.s: tasyāṃ suparṇāvadhi yau niviṣṭau tayordevānāmadhi bhāgadheyam ity abhimantrya
11.5.3.b.d: तस्यां सुपर्णावधि यौ निविष्टौ तयोर्देवानामधि भागधेयम् इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य
11.5.3.b.m: Upon whom the two eagles sit, [one of] whose shares among the gods is...': having addressed [it] with this [mantra],

11.5.4.a.m: twelve steps to the west of the pit (cātvāla) is the rubbish heap (utkara);

11.5.4.b.m: at the same distance to the north, just as the cātvāla [is placed].

11.5.5.a.m: The pit (cātvāla) and the high altar (uttaravedi) have been explained.

11.5.6.a.m: It remains covered overnight with udumbara branches or with plakṣa branches.

11.5.7.a.m: On the next day, he combines the last two Pravargya and Upasad rites:

11.5.8.a.m: having performed the morning ones, immediately thereupon the afternoon ones.

11.5.9.a.m: Here, having removed the Pravargya, he brings forward the fire as in the animal sacrifice.

11.5.10.b.m: the one from which he brings it forward is the gārhapatya.

11.5.11.a.m: While the fire is present, he traces the northern enclosing line.

11.5.12.a.s: atra pratiprathātā śākhāmāhṛtya maitrāvaruṇyāḥ payasyāyā vatsānapākaroti
11.5.12.a.d: अत्र प्रतिप्रथाता शाखामाहृत्य मैत्रावरुण्याः पयस्याया वत्सानपाकरोति
11.5.12.a.m: Here the pratiprasthātṛ, having brought a branch, keeps away the calves from [the cow giving milk for] the milk-curd preparation (payasyā) for Mitra and Varuṇa.

11.6.1.a.m: Having sprinkled the sacrificial grass, he sprinkles the altar ground three times.

11.6.2.a.m: They do not walk upon [an altar ground] that has not been sprinkled.

11.6.3.a.s: athaināṃ barhiṣā bahulaṃ prācīnam stīrtvā prayuktapūrve śakaṭe naddhayuge pratihataśamye prakṣālya tayoḥ prathamagrathitāngranthīnvisrasya navānprajñātānkṛtvāgreṇa prāgvaṃśamabhitaḥ pṛṣṭhyāmavyavanayanpariśrite sacchadiṣī avasthāpayati
11.6.3.a.d: अथैनां बर्हिषा बहुलं प्राचीनम् स्तीर्त्वा प्रयुक्तपूर्वे शकटे नद्धयुगे प्रतिहतशम्ये प्रक्षाल्य तयोः प्रथमग्रथितान्ग्रन्थीन्विस्रस्य नवान्प्रज्ञातान्कृत्वाग्रेण प्राग्वंशमभितः पृष्ठ्यामव्यवनयन्परिश्रिते सच्छदिषी अवस्थापयति
11.6.3.a.m: Then, having strewn it thickly with sacrificial grass pointing eastward, having washed the two carts that had been harnessed previously, whose yokes are bound, whose pegs are inserted, having untied their previously tied knots, having made new, recognizable ones, he sets up the two covered carts without letting them run off the spine, east of the eastern hall, surrounded on both sides of the spine by an enclosure.

11.6.4.a.m: Then the wife anoints the two [carts] with the third footprint [dust] mixed with clarified butter:

11.6.5.a.s: ā no vīro jāyatāmiti dvirdakṣiṇāmakṣadhuraṃ dakṣiṇena hastenottānena prācīnam
11.6.5.a.d: आ नो वीरो जायतामिति द्विर्दक्षिणामक्षधुरं दक्षिणेन हस्तेनोत्तानेन प्राचीनम्
11.6.5.a.m: twice on the southern axle-pole, with the right hand facing upwards, pointing eastward, with: 'May a hero be born to us...'

11.6.6.a.m: And she does not turn her hand.

11.6.9.a.m: In the same way she anoints the northern havirdhāna cart.

11.6.10.a.s: yuñjate mana iti sāvitriyarcauttaravedike hutvā havirdhānābhyāṃ pravartyamānābhyāmanubrūhīti saṃpreṣyati /
11.6.10.a.d: युञ्जते मन इति सावित्रियर्चौत्तरवेदिके हुत्वा हविर्धानाभ्यां प्रवर्त्यमानाभ्यामनुब्रूहीति संप्रेष्यति ।
11.6.10.a.m:
Having offered with the Savitṛ verse, "They harness the mind...", on the uttaravedi fire, [the adhvaryu] gives the call: "Recite for the two havirdhāna carts being rolled forward!"

Or: "Recite for the two being rolled forward!"

11.6.11.a.m: When the first [verse] has been recited three times, lifting [the carts], they roll them forward with: "Go forward to the sacrifice..."

11.6.12.a.m: If there should be the creaking of an axle, he should accompany it with the formula: "Of sweet voice..."

11.6.13.a.s: dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya vartmani vartmanīrvā hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ityadhvaryurhiraṇye juhoti
11.6.13.a.d: दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य वर्त्मनि वर्त्मनीर्वा हिरण्यं निधायेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्यध्वर्युर्हिरण्ये जुहोति
11.6.13.a.m: Having placed a piece of gold in the track or tracks of the southern havirdhāna cart, the adhvaryu offers upon the gold with: "This Viṣṇu strode across..."

11.6.14.a.m: In the same way the pratiprasthātṛ for the northern [cart].

11.7.1.a.m: He offers with: "Possessing food, possessing milk..."

11.7.2.a.s: apa janyaṃ bhayaṃ nudāpa cakrāṇi vartaya /
11.7.2.a.d: अप जन्यं भयं नुदाप चक्राणि वर्तय ।
11.7.2.a.m: "Drive away danger coming from strangers, drive away the wheels;

11.7.2.b.s: gṛhaṃ somasya gacchatamiti vitṛtīyadeśe vedyā adhvaryurhotā brahmā maitrāvaruṇo vā padāpanudati /
11.7.2.b.d: गृहं सोमस्य गच्छतमिति वितृतीयदेशे वेद्या अध्वर्युर्होता ब्रह्मा मैत्रावरुणो वा पदापनुदति ।
11.7.2.b.m: Go to the house of Soma"—at one-third of the altar ground, the adhvaryu, the hotṛ, the brahman, or the maitrāvaruṇa kicks away [a clod] with his foot.

11.7.2.c.m: Or he throws a clod outside the altar ground.

11.7.3.a.s: āhavanīyāttrīnpratīcaḥ prakramānucchiṣyātra ramethāmiti nabhyasthe sthāpayitvā vaiṣṇavamasi viṣṇustvottabhnātvityupastabhya divo vā viṣṇavityadhvaryurdakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya dakṣiṇaṃ kraṇātardamanu methīṃ nihanti /
11.7.3.a.d: आहवनीयात्त्रीन्प्रतीचः प्रक्रमानुच्छिष्यात्र रमेथामिति नभ्यस्थे स्थापयित्वा वैष्णवमसि विष्णुस्त्वोत्तभ्नात्वित्युपस्तभ्य दिवो वा विष्णवित्यध्वर्युर्दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य दक्षिणं क्रणातर्दमनु मेथीं निहन्ति ।
11.7.3.a.m: Leaving three steps west of the āhavanīya fire, having stopped them on their wheel-naves with: "Rest here...", having propped them up with: "You belong to Viṣṇu; may Viṣṇu prop you up", the adhvaryu drives a peg along the right wheel-perforation of the southern havirdhāna cart with: "Or from heaven, O Viṣṇu..."

11.7.4.a.m: In the same way the pratiprasthātṛ [binds the pole] along the northern wheel-perforation of the northern [cart] with: "Now of Viṣṇu..."

11.7.5.a.m: Pulling up the yoke-pins vertically, they wrap them from above.

11.7.6.a.m: For it is known [from scripture]: "Facing upwards, indeed, do the draft oxen of the gods carry."

11.7.7.a.s: maho vā viṣṇaviti sarvataḥ sthūṇāḥ pariminoti
11.7.7.a.d: महो वा विष्णविति सर्वतः स्थूणाः परिमिनोति
11.7.7.a.m: With: "Or from the great [realm], O Viṣṇu...", he sets up the posts on all sides.

11.7.8.a.m: Leaving space in front for the mound inside.

11.7.9.a.m: He places two beams pointing northward across, behind and in front.

11.7.10.a.m: A common line of sight belongs to the śālāmukhīya, the hotrīya, and the uttaravedika [fires].

11.8.1.a.s: viṣṇo rarāṭamasīti purastādrarāṭyāṃ tiryañcaṃ vaṃśaṃ dhārayanviṣṇoḥ syūrasīti syūtvā viṣṇordhruvamasīti prajñātaṃ granthiṃ kṛtvā prāco vaṃśānatyādhāya viṣṇoḥ pṛṣṭhamasīti teṣu madhyamaṃ chadiradhyūhati tryaratnivistāraṃ navāyāmam
11.8.1.a.d: विष्णो रराटमसीति पुरस्ताद्रराट्यां तिर्यञ्चं वंशं धारयन्विष्णोः स्यूरसीति स्यूत्वा विष्णोर्ध्रुवमसीति प्रज्ञातं ग्रन्थिं कृत्वा प्राचो वंशानत्याधाय विष्णोः पृष्ठमसीति तेषु मध्यमं छदिरध्यूहति त्र्यरत्निविस्तारं नवायामम्
11.8.1.a.m: Holding a crossbeam across the front gable with: "You are the forehead of Viṣṇu", sewing it on with: "You are the stitch of Viṣṇu", making a recognisable knot with: "You are the firm knot of Viṣṇu", placing beams pointing east across, he puts on the middle roof upon them with: "You are the back of Viṣṇu", three cubits in width and nine in length.

11.8.2.a.s: tūṣṇīmitare chadiṣī adhyūhya kaṭāṃstejanīriti chadyanatarāleṣu pravartamupāsyati
11.8.2.a.d: तूष्णीमितरे छदिषी अध्यूह्य कटांस्तेजनीरिति छद्यनतरालेषु प्रवर्तमुपास्यति
11.8.2.a.m: Having silently placed the other two roofs upon it, he fastens a border at the intervals between the roofs, [whispering]: "You are reed mats, you are points..."

11.8.4.a.s: pari tvā girvaṇo gira iti sarvataḥ pariśritya viṣṇoḥ śnaptre stha iti rarāṭyā aṃtau vyasyati /
11.8.4.a.d: परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इति सर्वतः परिश्रित्य विष्णोः श्नप्त्रे स्थ इति रराट्या अंतौ व्यस्यति ।
11.8.4.a.m: Having enclosed it on all sides with: "The songs have encompassed you, lover of song...", he spreads out the ends of the gable piece with: "You two are the jaws of Viṣṇu".

11.8.5.a.s: viṣṇoḥ syūrasītyadhvaryurdakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhuṃ syūtvā viṣṇordhruvamasīti prajñātaṃ granthiṃ karoti
11.8.5.a.d: विष्णोः स्यूरसीत्यध्वर्युर्दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुं स्यूत्वा विष्णोर्ध्रुवमसीति प्रज्ञातं ग्रन्थिं करोति
11.8.5.a.m: Sewing the southern doorpost with: "You are the stitch of Viṣṇu", the adhvaryu ties a recognisable knot with: "You are the firm knot of Viṣṇu".

11.8.6.a.m: Some teach the tying of the knot first.

11.8.7.a.s: yaṃ prathamaṃ granthiṃ grathnīyād ity uktam
11.8.7.a.d: यं प्रथमं ग्रन्थिं ग्रथ्नीयाद् इत्य् उक्तम्
11.8.7.a.m: "Whichever knot he would tie first..."—thus it is stated [in the Brāhmaṇa].

11.8.8.a.m: In the same way the pratiprasthātṛ [sews and ties] the northern [doorpost].

11.8.10.a.m: The havirdhāna shed is raised in the front and lowered behind.

11.8.11.a.m: With: "You belong to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu thee", he touches the shed.

11.9.1.a.s: pra tadviṣṇu stavate vīryāya mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ /
11.9.1.a.d: प्र तद्विष्णु स्तवते वीर्याय मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः ।
11.9.1.a.m: "For his heroic deed Viṣṇu is praised, like a dread beast wandering at will, mountain-dwelling,

11.9.1.b.s: yasyoruṣu triṣu vikramaṇeṣvadhikṣiyanti bhuvanāni viśveti saṃmitātprāṅ yajamāno niṣkramyāhavanīyāntrīnprācaḥ prakramānprakrāmati yasyoruṣviti
11.9.1.b.d: यस्योरुषु त्रिषु विक्रमणेष्वधिक्षियन्ति भुवनानि विश्वेति संमितात्प्राङ् यजमानो निष्क्रम्याहवनीयान्त्रीन्प्राचः प्रक्रमान्प्रक्रामति यस्योरुष्विति
11.9.1.b.m: In whose three wide strides all beings dwell"—with these words the sacrificer, stepping out eastward from the shed, takes three steps eastward from the āhavanīya fire, [concluding] with: "In whose wide [strides]..."

11.9.2.a.m: The adhvaryu should not pass eastward between the two havirdhāna carts.

11.9.3.a.m: If he should pass through, he should walk with a verse to Viṣṇu.

11.9.4.a.m: Six paces from the heap of rubbish towards the east he erects the āgnīdhra shed;

11.9.4.b.m: Half inside the altar ground, half outside the altar ground;

11.9.4.c.m: With its ridgepole pointing eastward, having four posts, enclosed on all sides, with its entrance to the south.

11.9.5.a.m: Three paces in front of the western boundary of the altar ground, he erects the sadas transversely.

11.9.7.a.m: Nine cubits in width and twenty-seven long towards the north;

11.9.8.a.m: "As much as he considers sufficient for the priests, the dhiṣṇya hearths, and the crawling attendants"—such is another rule.

11.9.9.a.s: dakṣiṇataḥ prakrame pṛṣṭhyāyā audumbarīṃ madhye sadaso minoti
11.9.9.a.d: दक्षिणतः प्रक्रमे पृष्ठ्याया औदुम्बरीं मध्ये सदसो मिनोति
11.9.9.a.m: One pace south of the spine line, he erects the audumbarī post in the middle of the sadas.

11.9.10.a.s: dakṣiṇā sadaḥ prati karṣedyathā sāṃkāśinasyāvirodhaṃ syāt
11.9.10.a.d: दक्षिणा सदः प्रति कर्षेद्यथा सांकाशिनस्याविरोधं स्यात्
11.9.10.a.m: He should pull the sadas toward the south so that there is no obstruction of the line of sight.

11.9.11.a.m: The preparation of the hole for the audumbarī post is like that for the sacrificial post, except for the chip.

11.9.12.a.s: agreṇāvaṭaṃ prācīṃ nidhāya tūṣṇīṃ prakṣālyāthaināṃ yavamatībhiḥ prokṣati /
11.9.12.a.d: अग्रेणावटं प्राचीं निधाय तूष्णीं प्रक्षाल्याथैनां यवमतीभिः प्रोक्षति ।
11.9.12.a.m: Having placed it east of the hole pointing eastward and washed it silently, he then sprinkles it with [water containing] barley grains:

11.9.13.a.m: With: "Prop up the sky, fill the atmosphere...", with its fork pointing eastward, he raises it together with the udgātṛ;

11.9.13.b.m: Or with: "Raise yourself, O tree, united with the divine barhis..."

11.10.1.a.s: dyutānastvā māruto minotviti prācīnakarṇāṃ sahodgātrā minoti
11.10.1.a.d: द्युतानस्त्वा मारुतो मिनोत्विति प्राचीनकर्णां सहोद्गात्रा मिनोति
11.10.1.a.m: With: "May the shining one, belonging to the Maruts, erect you", with its fork pointing eastward, he erects it together with the udgātṛ.

11.10.2.a.m: Above the buried portion, it is measured to the height of the sacrificer.

11.10.3.a.m: The heaping round, firming down, and sprinkling round are like those for the sacrificial post.

11.10.4.a.s: tasyā viśākhe hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī āpṛṇethāmiti sruveṇa hiraṇye juhvadāntamaudumbarīmanvavasrāvayati
11.10.4.a.d: तस्या विशाखे हिरण्यं निधाय घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी आपृणेथामिति स्रुवेण हिरण्ये जुह्वदान्तमौदुम्बरीमन्ववस्रावयति
11.10.4.a.m: Having placed a piece of gold in its fork, offering upon the gold with the dipping spoon with: "O Heaven and Earth, be filled with ghee...", he causes [the ghee] to flow down along the audumbarī post to its very end.

11.10.5.a.m: This is the tallest of the posts of the sadas.

11.10.7.a.m: One should erect the sadas low for someone desiring rain.

11.10.7.b.m: Some say: high for someone not desiring rain.

11.10.8.a.s: udañcaḥ prācaśca vaṃśānatyādhāyaindramasīti teṣu madhyamāni trīni chadīṃṣyadhyūhati
11.10.8.a.d: उदञ्चः प्राचश्च वंशानत्याधायैन्द्रमसीति तेषु मध्यमानि त्रीनि छदींष्यध्यूहति
11.10.8.a.m: Having placed crossbeams facing north and facing east, he puts upon them the three middle roof-mats with: “You are Indra's.”

11.10.9.a.m: The three southern ones with: “Shadow of all people.”

11.10.9.b.m: The three northern ones with: “You are Indra's seat.”

11.10.10.a.m: The southern and northern ones have their tips facing towards the audumbarī post.

11.10.11.a.m: It is taught in scripture: “He makes the southern ones over the northern ones.”

11.10.13.d.m: seventeen in a vājapeya and an atirātra;

11.10.14.a.m: The intervening spaces, the enclosing mats, the windows, and the two doors are as with the havirdhāna shed.

11.10.15.a.m: He sews it with: “You are Indra's seam.”

11.10.15.b.s: indrasya dhruvamasīti prajñātaṃ granthiṃ kṛtvaindramasīndrāya tveti saṃmitamabhimṛśati
11.10.15.b.d: इन्द्रस्य ध्रुवमसीति प्रज्ञातं ग्रन्थिं कृत्वैन्द्रमसीन्द्राय त्वेति संमितमभिमृशति
11.10.15.b.m: Having tied a well-known knot with: “You are Indra's firm [fastening],” he touches the measured [sadas] with: “You belong to Indra, for Indra [I touch] you.”

11.10.16.a.m: The adhvaryu should not pass westward through the sadas,

11.10.17.a.m: If he should pass, he should proceed with a verse addressed to Indra:

11.10.17.b.s: ā ghā ye agnimindhate stṛṇanti barhirānuṣak /
11.10.17.b.d: आ घा ये अग्निमिन्धते स्तृणन्ति बर्हिरानुषक् ।
11.10.17.b.m: “They who kindle the fire, who strew the sacrificial grass continuously,

11.10.17.c.m: whose youthful friend is Indra”—some teach this as the strewing verse.

11.10.18.a.m: Or he may proceed with a verse addressed to Kṣetrapatī.

11.10.19.a.m: Some teach the work on the sounding-holes first;

11.11.1.a.m: Under the southern havirdhāna cart, in front of the axle, he makes four sounding-holes at the intermediate points of the compass, a span wide in mouth and a span distant from one another.

11.11.2.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ityabhrimādāya parilikhitaṃ rakṣaḥ parilikhitā arātaya iti trirdakṣiṇapūrvaṃ parilikhati
11.11.2.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्यभ्रिमादाय परिलिखितं रक्षः परिलिखिता अरातय इति त्रिर्दक्षिणपूर्वं परिलिखति
11.11.2.a.m: Taking the spade with: “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ…,” he marks out the south-eastern one three times with: “Marked around is the demon, marked around are the enemies.”

11.11.3.a.m: In the same way, the others, keeping them clockwise and ending in the north.

11.11.4.a.m: In this regular order the subsequent rites are performed for them.

11.11.6.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ bāhumātrānkhātvā rakṣohaṇo valagahano vaiṣṇavānkhanāmīti khanati
11.11.6.a.d: तूष्णीं बाहुमात्रान्खात्वा रक्षोहणो वलगहनो वैष्णवान्खनामीति खनति
11.11.6.a.m: Having dug an arm's depth silently, he digs with: “Destroyers of demons, destroyers of hidden spells, belonging to Viṣṇu, I dig you.”

11.11.7.a.m: Some teach the formulas for the sounding-holes in the singular.

11.11.8.a.s: virāḍasīti bāhumupāvahṛtyedamahaṃ taṃ valagamudvapāmītyudupyoparavanyante 'vabādhate gāyatreṇa chandasāvabāḍho valaga iti
11.11.8.a.d: विराडसीति बाहुमुपावहृत्येदमहं तं वलगमुद्वपामीत्युदुप्योपरवन्यन्ते ऽवबाधते गायत्रेण छन्दसावबाढो वलग इति
11.11.8.a.m: Having inserted his arm with: “You are Virāj,” and having scooped out [earth] with: “Here I dig up that hidden spell,” he thrusts it down near the sounding-hole with: “The hidden spell is thrust down by the Gāyatrī meter.”

11.11.9.a.m: With: “I remove the ones belonging to Viṣṇu,” he removes [the earth].

11.11.9.b.m: With: “Thrust down is the malignant one,” he casts it down in front of the prop-stand.

11.11.11.b.m: Inserting his arm with each preceding formula, he thrusts down with each subsequent meter.

11.11.12.a.m: Gāyatra, Traiṣṭubha, Jāgata, Ānuṣṭubha, and Paṅkta are traditionally handed down.

11.12.2.a.s: virāḍasi sapatnahā bhrātṛvyahā svarāḍasyabhimātihā viśvārāḍasi viśvāsāṃ nāṣṭrāṇāṃ hanteti bāhū upāvaharato 'dhvaryuryajamānaśca
11.12.2.a.d: विराडसि सपत्नहा भ्रातृव्यहा स्वराडस्यभिमातिहा विश्वाराडसि विश्वासां नाष्ट्राणां हन्तेति बाहू उपावहरतो ऽध्वर्युर्यजमानश्च
11.12.2.a.m: With: “You are Virāj, slayer of rivals, slayer of enemies; you are Svarāj, slayer of the plotter; you are Viśvārāj, slayer of all destructive spirits,” the adhvaryu and the sacrificer both insert their arms.

11.12.3.a.s: saṃmṛśa imānāyuṣe varcase ca devānāṃ nidhirasi dveṣoyavanaḥ /
11.12.3.a.d: संमृश इमानायुषे वर्चसे च देवानां निधिरसि द्वेषोयवनः ।
11.12.3.a.m: “I touch these for life and for splendour; you are the treasure of the gods, warding off hatred.

11.12.3.b.m: Ward off from us whatever hatreds we have committed.

11.12.3.c.m: This which is the deposit of the gods, shine forth upon the four quarters,

11.12.3.d.d: कृण्वानो अन्याम्̐ अधरान्सपत्नानित्युपरवान्संमृश्य दक्षिणपूर्वं यजमानो ऽवमृशति ।
11.12.3.d.m: making other rivals base”—having touched the sounding-holes together, the sacrificer touches down into the south-eastern one;

11.12.3.e.m: the adhvaryu into the north-western one.

11.12.4.a.m: Then the sacrificer asks: “Adhvaryu, what is here?”

11.12.4.c.m: Saying: “May that be together for both of us,” the sacrificer touches down into the north-eastern one;

11.12.4.d.m: the adhvaryu into the south-western one.

11.12.4.e.m: The question and the answer are just the same.

11.12.4.f.m: “May that be mine,” says the sacrificer.

11.12.5.a.s: rakṣohaṇo valagahanaḥ prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavāniti yavamatībhiruparavānprokṣyottarairmantrairavanayāmīti prokṣaṇīśeṣamavaṭe 'vanīya yavo 'sīti yavamavāsyāvastṛṇāmīti barhiṣāvastīryābhijuhomītyājyenābhijuhoti
11.12.5.a.d: रक्षोहणो वलगहनः प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवानिति यवमतीभिरुपरवान्प्रोक्ष्योत्तरैर्मन्त्रैरवनयामीति प्रोक्षणीशेषमवटे ऽवनीय यवो ऽसीति यवमवास्यावस्तृणामीति बर्हिषावस्तीर्याभिजुहोमीत्याज्येनाभिजुहोति
11.12.5.a.m: Having sprinkled the sounding-holes with water containing barley with: “Destroyers of demons, destroyers of hidden spells, belonging to Viṣṇu, I sprinkle you,” he pours down the remainder of the sprinkling water into the pit with the subsequent formulas: “I pour down…,” puts in barley with: “You are barley,” strews them with sacrificial grass with: “I strew…,” and offers ghee upon them with: “I offer upon…”

11.12.7.a.s: rakṣohaṇau valagahanau prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavī ityadhiṣavaṇaphalake prokṣati
11.12.7.a.d: रक्षोहणौ वलगहनौ प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवी इत्यधिषवणफलके प्रोक्षति
11.12.7.a.m: He sprinkles the two pressing-boards with: “Destroyers of demons, destroyers of hidden spells, belonging to Viṣṇu, I sprinkle you two.”

11.13.1.a.s: audumbare kārṣmaryamaye pālāśe vā śuṣke taṣṭe pradhimukhe purastātsamāvikarte paścāt
11.13.1.a.d: औदुम्बरे कार्ष्मर्यमये पालाशे वा शुष्के तष्टे प्रधिमुखे पुरस्तात्समाविकर्ते पश्चात्
11.13.1.a.m: [They are] made of udumbara, kārṣmarya, or palāśa wood, dry, planed, shaped like wheel-rims in front, and cut straight at the back.

11.13.3.a.m: Or, he pierces them in the Ukthya and subsequent sacrifices.

11.13.4.a.s: athaine uparaveṣūpadadhāti rakṣohaṇau valagahanāvupadadhāmi vaiṣṇavī iti
11.13.4.a.d: अथैने उपरवेषूपदधाति रक्षोहणौ वलगहनावुपदधामि वैष्णवी इति
11.13.4.a.m: Then he sets the two [sound-boards] down over the sounding-holes with the formulas: “Slayers of the Rakṣases, slayers of sorcery, belonging to Viṣṇu, I set you two down.”

11.13.5.a.m: With the southern [board] he covers two;

11.13.6.a.m: Joined in front, they are two angulas apart at the back.

11.13.7.a.s: athaine uttarairmantraiḥ paryūhāmīti pradakṣiṇamuparavapāṃsubhiḥ paryuhya paristṛṇāmīti barhiṣā paristīryottamenābhimantrayate
11.13.7.a.d: अथैने उत्तरैर्मन्त्रैः पर्यूहामीति प्रदक्षिणमुपरवपांसुभिः पर्युह्य परिस्तृणामीति बर्हिषा परिस्तीर्योत्तमेनाभिमन्त्रयते
11.13.7.a.m: Then, having heaped around them with the dust from the sounding-holes in a clockwise direction with the following formulas: “I heap around...”, having strewn around with sacrificial grass with: “I strew around...”, he addresses them with the last [formula].

11.13.8.a.m: In front of the prop of this very cart of offerings, with the dust from the sounding-holes, he makes a square mound suitable for the soma cups.

11.13.9.a.m: In front he leaves a pathway.

11.13.10.a.m: Between the cātvāla and the utkara, or between the āgnīdhra and the cātvāla, the adhvaryu and those who wish to see may move.

11.13.11.a.s: sarvataḥ prasute dṛśīkavaḥ saṃcareyur ity eke
11.13.11.a.d: सर्वतः प्रसुते दृशीकवः संचरेयुर् इत्य् एके
11.13.11.a.m: “When [the soma] is pressed, those who wish to see may move on all sides,” say some.

11.14.1.a.m: From the cātvāla he heaps up the dhiṣṇya hearths.

11.14.2.a.s: antarāgnīdhra āgnīdhrīyamuttare vedyanta uttarataḥ saṃcaraṃ śiṣṭvā
11.14.2.a.d: अन्तराग्नीध्र आग्नीध्रीयमुत्तरे वेद्यन्त उत्तरतः संचरं शिष्ट्वा
11.14.2.a.m: Inside the āgnīdhra shed [he heaps] the āgnīdhra hearth at the northern edge of the altar ground, having left a pathway to the north;

11.14.3.a.m: the others in the eastern half of the sadas, having left a pathway in front;

11.14.4.b.m: to the south of it, the praśāstṛ's hearth.

11.14.5.a.m: To the north of the hotṛ's hearth, he arranges the others towards the north;

11.14.5.b.m: [namely,] those of the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the potṛ, the neṣṭṛ, and the acchāvāka.

11.14.6.a.s: bahiḥ sadaso mārjālīyaṃ dakṣiṇe vedyante dakṣiṇataḥ saṃcaraṃ śiṣṭvā samamāgnīdhrīyeṇa
11.14.6.a.d: बहिः सदसो मार्जालीयं दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते दक्षिणतः संचरं शिष्ट्वा सममाग्नीध्रीयेण
11.14.6.a.m: Outside the sadas, [he heaps] the mārjālīya hearth at the southern edge of the altar ground, having left a pathway to the south, aligned with the āgnīdhra hearth.

11.14.7.a.m: [He heaps them] with the eight [formulas] beginning with “You are all-pervading...”, each with its own formula.

11.14.8.a.m: Some teach these very formulas for the reverencing and for the sprinkling with clarified butter.

11.14.9.a.s: anudiśatītarānadhvanāmadhvapate namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīriti taṃtamabhikrāmam
11.14.9.a.d: अनुदिशतीतरानध्वनामध्वपते नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरिति तंतमभिक्रामम्
11.14.9.a.m: He assigns the others, stepping towards each in turn with: “O lord of the ways, homage be to you! Do not injure me!”

11.14.10.a.m: [He assigns] the āhavanīya fire with: “You are sovereign ruler, Kṛśānu.”

11.14.10.b.m: [He assigns] the place of the bahiṣpavamāna chant with: “You are the member of the assembly, pavamāna.”

11.14.10.c.m: [He assigns] the cātvāla with: “You are swift, cloudy.”

11.14.10.d.m: [He assigns] the slaughtering place with: “You are unwiped, provider of oblations.”

11.14.10.e.m: [He assigns] the rubbish heap with: “You are to be gathered together, all-bearing.”

11.14.10.f.m: [He assigns] the udumbara post with: “You are of sacred order, heavenly light.”

11.15.1.a.m: [He assigns] the brahman priest with: “You are the light of sacred knowledge, heavenly abode.”

11.15.1.b.m: [He assigns] the sadasya with: “You are an attendee of the sadas, robber.”

11.15.1.c.m: [He assigns] the sadas with: “You are the ocean, all-bearing.”

11.15.1.d.m: [He assigns] the śālāmukhīya fire with: “You are Aja Ekapād.”

11.15.1.e.m: [He assigns] the prājahita fire with: “You are Ahi Budhnya.”

11.15.1.f.m: [He assigns] the dakṣiṇāgni fire with: “You are the funeral offering, the bearer of funeral offerings.”

11.15.1.g.s: āyurbṛhattadaśīy tanmāvatu tasya nāmnā vṛścāmi yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ /
11.15.1.g.d: आयुर्बृहत्तदशीय् तन्मावतु तस्य नाम्ना वृश्चामि यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः ।
11.15.1.g.m: “Lifespan is the Bṛhat [sāman]; may I obtain that; may that protect me; by its name I cut off him who hates us and whom we hate.”

11.15.1.h.s: viśvāyurvāmadevyaṃ tadaśīya tanmāvatu tasya nāmnā vṛścāmi yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayamā dviṣmaḥ /
11.15.1.h.d: विश्वायुर्वामदेव्यं तदशीय तन्मावतु तस्य नाम्ना वृश्चामि यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयमा द्विष्मः ।
11.15.1.h.m: “All life is the Vāmadevya [sāman]; may I obtain that; may that protect me; by its name I cut off him who hates us and whom we hate.”

11.15.1.i.s: āyuḥpati rathamtaraṃ tadaśīya tanmāvatu tasya nāmnā vṛścāmi yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma ityetaiśca pratimantraṃ havirdhānāgnīdhrasadāṃsīti
11.15.1.i.d: आयुःपति रथम्तरं तदशीय तन्मावतु तस्य नाम्ना वृश्चामि यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इत्येतैश्च प्रतिमन्त्रं हविर्धानाग्नीध्रसदांसीति
11.15.1.i.m: “The lord of life is the Rathantara [sāman]; may I obtain that; may that protect me; by its name I cut off him who hates us and whom we hate.” And with these formulas, each with its own formula, [he assigns] the two cart-sheds, the āgnīdhra shed, and the sadas.

11.15.2.a.m: He attaches “with the fierce face” everywhere.

11.15.3.a.s: stṛṇīta barhiḥ pra vrataṃ yacchateti saṃpreṣyati
11.15.3.a.d: स्तृणीत बर्हिः प्र व्रतं यच्छतेति संप्रेष्यति
11.15.3.a.m: He issues the ritual call: “Strew the sacrificial grass; bring forward the fast-milk!”

11.15.4.a.s: pūrvasmin vā staraṇa etaṃ saṃpraiṣaṃ brūyāt
11.15.4.a.d: पूर्वस्मिन् वा स्तरण एतं संप्रैषं ब्रूयात्
11.15.4.a.m: Or, he should utter this ritual call at the earlier strewing.

11.15.5.a.m: Strewing here, he should not strew over the uttaravedi, the mound, the sounding-holes, or the dhiṣṇya hearths.

11.15.6.a.m: Here, he gives one teat of fast-milk to the sacrificer.

11.15.7.a.m: Here, the Vājasaneyins prescribe half the fast-milk;

11.15.7.b.m: [and] half between the last Pravargya and Upasad rites.

11.16.1.a.m: He begins the procedure of the animal sacrifice for Agni and Soma.

11.16.2.a.m: Its ritual procedure is like that of the independent animal sacrifice.

11.16.3.a.m: The sixfold formula and the animal iṣṭi do not occur in sacrifices that form subsidiary rites.

11.16.4.a.m: Silently he binds together the sacrificial grass of the hospitality rite;

11.16.5.a.m: and those enclosing sticks into the firewood bundle of the animal sacrifice.

11.16.6.a.m: At the time of setting down the vessels, he prepares the pracaraṇī ladle as the seventh.

11.16.8.a.s: ājyagrahaṇakāle pracarṇyāmāditastūṣṇīṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā pāśukānyājyāni gṛhṇāti
11.16.8.a.d: आज्यग्रहणकाले प्रचर्ण्यामादितस्तूष्णीं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा पाशुकान्याज्यानि गृह्णाति
11.16.8.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, having first taken four ladlings silently in the pracaraṇī ladle, he takes the clarified butter portions for the animal sacrifice.

11.16.9.a.m: With: “May the wife of the brahman priest go forward...”, the pratiprasthātṛ brings forward the wife.

11.16.10.a.s: athāhamanukāminīti patnī śālāmukhīyamupopaviśya suprajasastvā vayamiti japati
11.16.10.a.d: अथाहमनुकामिनीति पत्नी शालामुखीयमुपोपविश्य सुप्रजसस्त्वा वयमिति जपति
11.16.10.a.m: Sitting down beside the śālāmukhīya fire with: “Now I, desirous of following...”, the wife mutters: “May we be having good offspring...”

11.16.11.a.m: The brahman priest places the king [Soma] on his lap.

11.16.12.a.m: He issues the ritual call: “Summon those who share the vow!”

11.16.13.a.m: They summon the members of the sacrificer's household.

11.16.14.a.m: The sacrificer holds onto the adhvaryu from behind;

11.16.14.c.m: the others—the sons and brothers—onto the wife.

11.16.15.a.s: ahatena vāsasāmātyānsaṃpracchādya vāsaso 'nte srugdaṇḍamupaniyamya pracarṇyā vaisarjanāni juhoti
11.16.15.a.d: अहतेन वाससामात्यान्संप्रच्छाद्य वाससो ऽन्ते स्रुग्दण्डमुपनियम्य प्रचर्ण्या वैसर्जनानि जुहोति
11.16.15.a.m: Having covered the household members completely with an unwashed garment, and having gripped the handle of the ladle at the edge of the garment, he offers the vaisarjana oblations with the pracaraṇī ladle.

11.16.16.a.s: tvaṃ soma tanūkṛdbhyo juṣāṇa ityetābhyāmardhaṃ gārhapatye
11.16.16.a.d: त्वं सोम तनूकृद्भ्यो जुषाण इत्येताभ्यामर्धं गार्हपत्ये
11.16.16.a.m: With the two [verses], “You, O Soma, enjoying from the makers of bodies…,” he offers half [the clarified butter] into the gārhapatya.

11.17.1.a.m: [They take up] the pressing-stones, the Vāyu-cups, and the trough.

11.17.1.d.m: For a nomadic sacrificer, they roll forward those that are at the other gārhapatya.

11.17.1.f.m: They carry along after: firewood, sacrificial grass, clarified butter, and the sprinkling waters.

11.17.2.a.m:
Having kindled the firewood for the carrying-forward at the śālāmukhīya [fire], and having supported it with sand, he calls out: “Recite for the two being carried forward, Agni and Soma!”

Or [he calls out]: “Recite for the two being carried forward!”

11.17.3.a.s: prathamāyāṃ triranūktāyāmayaṃ no agnirvarivaḥ kṛṇotvityagniprathamāḥ somaprathamā vā prāñco 'bhipravrajanti
11.17.3.a.d: प्रथमायां त्रिरनूक्तायामयं नो अग्निर्वरिवः कृणोत्वित्यग्निप्रथमाः सोमप्रथमा वा प्राञ्चो ऽभिप्रव्रजन्ति
11.17.3.a.m: When the first [verse] has been recited thrice, they step forward towards the east with “May this Agni make broad room for us…,” with Agni first, or with Soma first.

11.17.4.a.m: Having set down the fire in the āgnīdhrīya [fire-shed], he offers half of the remainder of the clarified butter with “O Agni, lead…!”

11.17.5.a.m: He deposits the pressing-stones, the Vāyu-cups, and the trough in the āgnīdhra [shed] for the night.

11.17.6.a.s: uttareṇāgnīdhrīyamāhavanīyaṃ gatvoru viṣṇo vikramasveti sarvamājyaśeṣaṃ juhoti
11.17.6.a.d: उत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयमाहवनीयं गत्वोरु विष्णो विक्रमस्वेति सर्वमाज्यशेषं जुहोति
11.17.6.a.m: Having gone north of the āgnīdhrīya to the āhavanīya, he offers the entire remainder of the clarified butter with “Stride broadly, O Viṣṇu…!”

11.17.7.a.m: When it has been offered, the attendants, having turned clockwise, return the way they came.

11.17.8.a.s: somo jigāti gātuvidityaparayā dvārā havirdhānaṃ rājānaṃ prapādayati /
11.17.8.a.d: सोमो जिगाति गातुविदित्यपरया द्वारा हविर्धानं राजानं प्रपादयति ।
11.17.8.a.m: With “Soma goes knowing the way…,” he brings King [Soma] into the havirdhāna [shed] through the western door.

11.17.9.a.m: The sacrificer enters through the eastern [door].

11.17.10.a.m: In the seat of the southern havirdhāna [cart], the spreading of the black antelope skin and the placing of King [Soma] take place as before.

11.18.1.a.s: athainaṃ yajamāno devatābhyaḥ saṃprayacchatyeṣa vo deva savitaḥ soma iti
11.18.1.a.d: अथैनं यजमानो देवताभ्यः संप्रयच्छत्येष वो देव सवितः सोम इति
11.18.1.a.m: Then the sacrificer hands him over to the deities with “This is your soma, O divine Savitṛ…!”

11.18.2.a.s: etattvaṃ soma devo devānupāgā ityabhimantryedamahaṃ manuṣyo manuṣyāniti pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya namo devebhya iti prācīnamañjaliṃ kṛtvā svadhā pitṛbhya iti dakṣiṇedamahaṃ nirvaruṇasya pāśādityupaniṣkramya svarabhivyakhyamiti prāṅ prekṣate /
11.18.2.a.d: एतत्त्वं सोम देवो देवानुपागा इत्यभिमन्त्र्येदमहं मनुष्यो मनुष्यानिति प्रदक्षिणमावृत्य नमो देवेभ्य इति प्राचीनमञ्जलिं कृत्वा स्वधा पितृभ्य इति दक्षिणेदमहं निर्वरुणस्य पाशादित्युपनिष्क्रम्य स्वरभिव्यख्यमिति प्राङ् प्रेक्षते ।
11.18.2.a.m: Having addressed him with “Thus, O Soma, you as a god have approached the gods,” [and saying] “Here I as a mortal [approach] mortals,” having turned clockwise, having made añjali facing east with “Homage to the gods,” and facing south with “Svadhā to the fathers,” having stepped out with “Here I [escape] from Varuṇa’s noose,” he looks towards the east with “I have beheld the light.”

11.18.2.b.m: Or [with the words]: “May I behold heaven.”

11.18.2.c.m: He gazes over the entire sacrificial precinct.

11.18.3.a.m: Here the sacrificer releases the intermediate consecration.

11.18.4.a.m: He reverences the āhavanīya with “O Agni, lord of vows, you are the lord of vows of vows…”

11.18.4.b.m: With this very [verse] he places a kindling-stick upon it, so [says] the Vājasaneyaka.

11.18.6.a.m: Some teachers prescribe the giving away of the staff at this point.

11.18.7.a.s: svāhā yajñaṃ manasā svāhā dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ svāhororantarikṣātsvāhā yajñaṃ vātādārabha iti muṣṭī visṛjate
11.18.7.a.d: स्वाहा यज्ञं मनसा स्वाहा द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां स्वाहोरोरन्तरिक्षात्स्वाहा यज्ञं वातादारभ इति मुष्टी विसृजते
11.18.7.a.m: He releases his fists with “Svāhā, the sacrifice with the mind; svāhā, to Heaven and Earth; svāhā, from the broad atmosphere; svāhā, I commence the sacrifice from the wind!”

11.18.8.a.s: svāhā vāci vāte visṛja iti vācam
11.18.8.a.d: स्वाहा वाचि वाते विसृज इति वाचम्
11.18.8.a.m: He releases speech with “Svāhā, release into speech, into the wind!”

11.18.10.a.m: He consumes the somas [and] the remainders of the oblations on the day of pressing.

11.18.11.a.m: He deposits the firewood and the sacrificial grass north of the āhavanīya, pointing east.

11.18.11.b.m: The firewood to the south, the sacrificial grass to the north.

11.19.1.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the consecration of the sprinkling waters.

11.19.2.a.m: At the time of strewing, he strews sacrificial grass west of the uttara-vedi.

11.19.4.a.s: ājyānāṃ sādanādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyate samānamā pravarāt
11.19.4.a.d: आज्यानां सादनादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यते समानमा प्रवरात्
11.19.4.a.m: He undertakes the animal-sacrifice rites beginning with the depositing of the clarified butter, which are identical up to the choice of priests.

11.19.5.a.s: daivaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ ca hotārau vṛtvāśrāvamāśrāvamṛtupraiṣādibhiḥ saumikānṛtvijo vṛṇīte
11.19.5.a.d: दैवं च मानुषं च होतारौ वृत्वाश्रावमाश्रावमृतुप्रैषादिभिः सौमिकानृत्विजो वृणीते
11.19.5.a.m: Having chosen the divine and the human hotṛs, having called out repeatedly, he chooses the soma-ritual officiating priests by means of the seasonal calls and so forth:

11.19.6.a.s: indraṃ hotrātsajūrdiva ā pṛthivyā iti hotāram
11.19.6.a.d: इन्द्रं होत्रात्सजूर्दिव आ पृथिव्या इति होतारम्
11.19.6.a.m: The hotṛ with “Indra from the hotṛ-office, together with Heaven and Earth…”;

11.19.7.a.m: having cast down a blade of grass without the wooden sword, the subsequent ones:

11.19.8.a.m: the agnīdh with “Agni from the agnīdhra-office…”;

11.19.8.b.m: the two adhvaryus with “The two Aśvins, the two adhvaryus, from the adhvaryu-office…”;

11.19.8.c.m: the maitrāvaruṇa with “Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, from the director’s office…”;

11.19.8.d.m: the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with “Indra, the brahman, from the brāhmaṇa’s office…”;

11.19.8.e.m: the potṛ with “The Maruts from the potṛ-office…”;

11.19.8.f.m: the neṣṭṛ with “The wives of the gods from the neṣṭṛ-office…”;

11.19.8.g.s: agnirdaivīnāṃ viśāṃ puraetāyaṃ yajamāno manuṣyāṇāṃ tayornāvasthūri gārhapatyaṃ dīdayacchataṃ himā dvā yū rādhāṃsītsaṃpṛñcānāvasaṃpṛñcānau tanva iti yajamānam
11.19.8.g.d: अग्निर्दैवीनां विशां पुरएतायं यजमानो मनुष्याणां तयोर्नावस्थूरि गार्हपत्यं दीदयच्छतं हिमा द्वा यू राधांसीत्संपृञ्चानावसंपृञ्चानौ तन्व इति यजमानम्
11.19.8.g.m: the sacrificer with “Agni is the leader of the divine clans; this sacrificer of the human; may their gārhapatya shine, not one-sided, for a hundred winters, both uniting their wealth, not uniting their bodies!”;

11.19.9.a.m: or with “This pressing sacrificer of the human…”

11.19.10.a.m: Some teachers prescribe the choice [of priests] at the animal sacrifice for the pressing day.

11.19.10.b.m: In that case, he should say “pressing [sacrificer].”

11.19.11.a.m: The utterance of the name is whispered everywhere.

11.20.1.a.s: pravṛtaḥpravṛtaḥ pravṛtahomau juhoti juṣṭo vāco bhūyāsamṛcā stomaṃ samardhayetyetābhyām
11.20.1.a.d: प्रवृतःप्रवृतः प्रवृतहोमौ जुहोति जुष्टो वाचो भूयासमृचा स्तोमं समर्धयेत्येताभ्याम्
11.20.1.a.m: Each chosen [priest] offers the two election-offerings with the two [verses]: “May I be pleasing to Speech…,” and “Prosper the chant through the verse…!”

11.20.2.a.m: Having performed [the rites] by day up to the fore-offerings, they attend upon the setting [sun] with the after-offerings.

11.20.3.a.s: hutāyāṃ vapāyāṃ mārjayitvā subrahmaṇya pitāputrīyāṃ subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti saṃpreṣyati
11.20.3.a.d: हुतायां वपायां मार्जयित्वा सुब्रह्मण्य पितापुत्रीयां सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति संप्रेष्यति
11.20.3.a.m: When the omentum has been offered, after having purified himself, he issues the command: "Subrahmaṇya, chant the Subrahmaṇyā formula mentioning father and son!"

11.20.4.a.m: From this point on, the Subrahmaṇyā formula indeed mentions father and son.

11.20.5.a.s: āhūtāyāṃ vasatīvarīḥ kumbhena giribhidāṃ vahantīnāṃ prayaṅtiṣṭhangṛhṇāti
11.20.5.a.d: आहूतायां वसतीवरीः कुम्भेन गिरिभिदां वहन्तीनां प्रयङ्तिष्ठन्गृह्णाति
11.20.5.a.m: When it has been chanted, standing facing east, he draws the Vasatīvarī waters with a pitcher from flowing [waters] that break the mountains.

11.20.6.a.m: He should not cross over the nearest flowing [waters].

11.20.7.a.m: He draws [them] at the junction of shade and sunshine.

11.20.8.a.s: yadyabhicchāyāṃ na vindedātmano vṛkṣasya kūlasya vā chāyāyām
11.20.8.a.d: यद्यभिच्छायां न विन्देदात्मनो वृक्षस्य कूलस्य वा छायायाम्
11.20.8.a.m: If he should not find shade, [he draws them] in the shade of himself, of a tree, or of a bank.

11.20.9.a.m: Making [the vessel] move against the current, he draws them with: "These waters, possessing oblation..."

11.20.10.a.s: yasyāgṛhītā abhinimrocetsuvarna gharmaḥ svāheti pañcārkāhutīrhutvā vare datta ulkāmupariṣṭāddhārayamāṇo gṛhṇīyāt /
11.20.10.a.d: यस्यागृहीता अभिनिम्रोचेत्सुवर्न घर्मः स्वाहेति पञ्चार्काहुतीर्हुत्वा वरे दत्त उल्कामुपरिष्टाद्धारयमाणो गृह्णीयात् ।
11.20.10.a.m: If the sun should set on him when they are not yet drawn, having offered five Arka-oblations with: "Svar, not the heat, svāhā!", having given a boon, he should draw them holding a torch above [the water].

11.20.11.a.s: yo vā brāhmkaṇo bahuyājī tasya kumbhyānāṃ gṛhṇīyāt
11.20.11.a.d: यो वा ब्राह्म्कणो बहुयाजी तस्य कुम्भ्यानां गृह्णीयात्
11.20.11.a.m: Or he should draw from the pitcher of a Brahmin who has performed many sacrifices.

11.20.12.a.m: "One who has performed a soma sacrifice is a performer of many sacrifices," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

11.20.13.a.m: He sets [the pitcher] down west of the śālāmukhīya fire with: "I set you down in the seat of Agni whose house has not fallen."

11.20.13.b.s: sumnāya sumninīḥ sumne mā dhatteti sarveṣu vasatīvarīṇāṃsādaneṣu yajamāno japati /
11.20.13.b.d: सुम्नाय सुम्निनीः सुम्ने मा धत्तेति सर्वेषु वसतीवरीणांसादनेषु यजमानो जपति ।
11.20.13.b.m: At every setting down of the Vasatīvarī waters, the sacrificer mutters: "Gracious ones, for grace, place me in grace!"

11.20.13.c.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the setting out of the vessels for the animal cake of the animal dedicated to Agni and Soma.

11.20.14.a.m: The sacrificer does not eat of [the cake] dedicated to Agni and Soma.

11.20.15.b.m: He does not remove the heart-spit.

11.20.16.a.m: The [sacrifice of the animal] dedicated to Agni and Soma concludes with the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

11.21.1.a.s: niśāyāṃ vasatīvarīḥ pariharatyantarvedyāsīne yajamāne patnyāṃ ca
11.21.1.a.d: निशायां वसतीवरीः परिहरत्यन्तर्वेद्यासीने यजमाने पत्न्यां च
11.21.1.a.m: At night, while the sacrificer and his wife are seated inside the altar ground, he carries the Vasatīvarī waters around.

11.21.2.a.m: He should not carry them around past one who is not consecrated.

11.21.3.a.s: savye 'ṃse 'tyādhāyāpareṇa prājahitaṃ parikramya pūrvayā dvāropanirhṛtya dakṣiṇena vediṃ gatvā dakṣiṇena mārjālīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parītya dakṣiṇasyāmuttaravediśroṇyāṃ sādayatīndrāgniyorbhāgadheyī stheti
11.21.3.a.d: सव्ये ऽंसे ऽत्याधायापरेण प्राजहितं परिक्रम्य पूर्वया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्य दक्षिणेन वेदिं गत्वा दक्षिणेन मार्जालीयं धिष्णियं परीत्य दक्षिणस्यामुत्तरवेदिश्रोण्यां सादयतीन्द्राग्नियोर्भागधेयी स्थेति
11.21.3.a.m: Having placed [the pitcher] on his left shoulder, having walked around west of the prājahita [fire], having carried it out through the eastern door, having gone south of the altar ground, having walked around south of the mārjālīya dhiṣṇya, he sets it down on the southern hip of the uttaravedi with: "You are the portion of Indra and Agni."

11.21.4.a.s: dakṣiṇe 'ṃse 'tyādhāya yathetaṃ gatvā pūrvayā dvāropahirhṛtyottareṇa vediṃ gatvottareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parītyottarasyāmuttaravediśroṇyāṃ sādayati mitrāvaruṇayorbhagadheyī stheti
11.21.4.a.d: दक्षिणे ऽंसे ऽत्याधाय यथेतं गत्वा पूर्वया द्वारोपहिर्हृत्योत्तरेण वेदिं गत्वोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं धिष्णियं परीत्योत्तरस्यामुत्तरवेदिश्रोण्यां सादयति मित्रावरुणयोर्भगधेयी स्थेति
11.21.4.a.m: Having placed it on his right shoulder, having gone back the way he came, having carried it out through the eastern door, having gone north of the altar ground, having walked around north of the āgnīdhra dhiṣṇya, he sets it down on the northern hip of the uttaravedi with: "You are the portion of Mitra and Varuṇa."

11.21.5.a.s: savye 'ṃse 'tyādhāya yathetaṃ gatvāpareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyamupasādayati viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ bhāgadheyī stheti
11.21.5.a.d: सव्ये ऽंसे ऽत्याधाय यथेतं गत्वापरेणाग्नीध्रीयं धिष्णियमुपसादयति विश्वेषां देवानां भागधेयी स्थेति
11.21.5.a.m: Having placed it on his left shoulder, having gone back the way he came, he sets it down west of the āgnīdhra dhiṣṇya with: "You are the portion of the All-gods."

11.21.6.a.m: When they have been set down, he addresses them with: "Watch over the sacrifice!"

11.21.7.a.m: At this point the pratiprasthātṛ causes the evening milking to be done for the sake of the curdled milk.

11.21.8.a.s: adhvaryuḥ saṃpreṣyati yā yajamānasya vratadhuktasyā āśiraṃ kuruta yā patniyai tasyai dadhigrahāya yā gharmadhuktasyai dadhigharmāya taptamanātaktaṃ maitrāvaruṇāya śṛtātaṅkyaṃ dadhi kurutādityagrahāya subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvaya na sadasyupavastavā iti
11.21.8.a.d: अध्वर्युः संप्रेष्यति या यजमानस्य व्रतधुक्तस्या आशिरं कुरुत या पत्नियै तस्यै दधिग्रहाय या घर्मधुक्तस्यै दधिघर्माय तप्तमनातक्तं मैत्रावरुणाय शृतातङ्क्यं दधि कुरुतादित्यग्रहाय सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वय न सदस्युपवस्तवा इति
11.21.8.a.m: The adhvaryu gives the command: "Make the milk-mixture from that [cow] which is the vow-cow of the sacrificer; for the dadhigraha from that [cow] of the wife; for the dadhigharma from that [cow] which is the milk-cow for the gharma; make heated, uncurdled [milk] for the Maitrāvaruṇa [cup]; make boiled, curdled milk for the Āditya cup; Subrahmaṇya, chant the Subrahmaṇyā formula; let there be no sleeping in the sadas!"

11.21.9.a.m: They act according to the command.

11.21.10.a.m: At this point he binds together the firewood and sacrificial grass of the savanīya [animal] or of the savanīya [animals].

11.21.12.a.m: They keep the sacrificer awake in the Āgnīdhra shed or in the Havirdhāna shed;

11.21.13.a.m: The officiating priests dwell this night in the Āgnīdhra shed.

12.1.1.a.m: Having awakened in the dead of night, he touches the āgnīdhra [fire or hearth] with: "O Agni, lead..."

12.1.2.a.m: The Havirdhāna shed with: "Viṣṇu strode across this..."

12.1.2.b.m: The ladles with: "O Agni, you purify our life-spans..."

12.1.2.c.s: ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā iti vāyavyāni /
12.1.2.c.d: आ वायो भूष शुचिपा इति वायव्यानि ।
12.1.2.c.m: The vāyavya cups with: "Come, O Vāyu, drink the pure [soma]..."

12.1.2.d.s: ā ghā ye agnimindhata iti sadaḥ
12.1.2.d.d: आ घा ये अग्निमिन्धत इति सदः
12.1.2.d.m: The sadas with: "Those indeed who kindle Agni..."

12.1.3.a.m: With: "Prajāpati through his mind... sought the soma plant," he offers the thirty-three Yajñatanū oblations into the āgnīdhra [fire].

12.1.3.b.m: Having offered with the first mantra, reciting each previous one in succession, he offers with each subsequent one.

12.1.4.a.m: The vāyavya cups are a span in length, with high rims, having pouring hollows on top, and constricted in the middle.

12.1.5.a.m: Those among them whose wood is not specified should be made of vikankata wood;

12.1.5.b.m: or of any sacrificial tree that bears fruit.

12.1.6.a.s: ko vo yunakti sa vo yunaktviti khare pātrāṇi prayunakti yānyanāmnātamantrāṇi bhavanti
12.1.6.a.d: को वो युनक्ति स वो युनक्त्विति खरे पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति यान्यनाम्नातमन्त्राणि भवन्ति
12.1.6.a.m: With: "Who yokes you? May he yoke you!" he arranges on the mound the cups for which no mantra has been handed down.

12.1.7.a.m: With: "Agni is the deity," [he sets] the Upāṃśu cup on the southern shoulder [of the mound].

12.1.8.a.m: With: "Soma is the deity," the Antaryāma cup on the northern [shoulder].

12.1.9.a.s: bṛhannasīti te antareṇa grāvāṇamupāṃśusavanaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaṃ saṃspṛṣṭaṃ pātrābhyām
12.1.9.a.d: बृहन्नसीति ते अन्तरेण ग्रावाणमुपांशुसवनं दक्षिणामुखं संस्पृष्टं पात्राभ्याम्
12.1.9.a.m: With: "You are great," between them [he places] the Upāṃśusavana pressing stone facing south, in contact with both cups.

12.1.10.a.m: West of it, facing west, [he sets] the cups for two deities:

12.1.11.a.m: With: "Indra is the deity," the cup for Indra and Vāyu, having a circumference [running round it];

12.1.11.b.m: with: "Bṛhaspati is the deity," the ajagāva cup for Mitra and Varuṇa;

12.1.11.c.m: with: "The Aśvins are the deities," the two-cornered cup for the Aśvins.

12.1.12.a.m: West of them, in a row side by side, [he sets] the cups of Śukra and Manthin:

12.1.12.b.m: with: "Sūrya is the deity," the southern one made of bilva wood for Śukra;

12.1.12.c.m: with: "The Moon is the deity," the northern one made of vikankata wood for Manthin.

12.1.13.a.s: te apareṇa prabāhugṛtupātre āśvatthe aśvaśaphabudhne ubhayatomukhe /
12.1.13.a.d: ते अपरेण प्रबाहुगृतुपात्रे आश्वत्थे अश्वशफबुध्ने उभयतोमुखे ।
12.1.13.a.m: West of them, in a row side by side, [he sets] the two Ṛtu cups made of aśvattha wood, shaped at the bottom like a horse's hoof, and having openings at both ends:

12.1.13.c.m: The latter [verse] is for the pratiprasthātṛ.

12.1.14.a.m: With “The All-Gods are the deity,” [he places] the āgrayaṇa-vessel on the southern hip;

12.1.14.b.m: with “Indra is the deity,” the ukthya-vessel on the northern;

12.1.14.c.m: and the ukthya cup to the north of it.

12.1.15.a.m: Between the two jars [he places] three atigrāhya vessels pointing northward,

12.1.15.b.m: namely, for Agni, for Indra, and for Sūrya.

12.2.1.a.m: On the northern shoulder [he places] the vessel for the curd draught, made of udumbara wood and four-cornered.

12.2.2.a.m: Of this very form are [the vessels] for the Aṃśu and Adābhya [draughts].

12.2.3.a.m: If he draws a soma draught, this very [vessel] may serve.

12.2.4.a.m: In front of the prop of this very havirdhāna [cart he places] the Āditya jar,

12.2.4.b.m: and north of it the Āditya vessel.

12.2.5.a.m: With "Earth is the deity," [he places] the Dhruva jar in front of the prop of the northern havirdhāna [cart], on an unheaped [spot].

12.2.6.a.s: khare ṣoḍaśipātraṃ khādiraṃ catuḥsrakti yadi ṣoḍaśī
12.2.6.a.d: खरे षोडशिपात्रं खादिरं चतुःस्रक्ति यदि षोडशी
12.2.6.a.m: On the mound [he places] the Ṣoḍaśin vessel, made of khadira wood and four-cornered, if there is a Ṣoḍaśin.

12.2.7.a.m: In the middle [he places] the pariplavā ladle, formed like a ladling spoon without a handle.

12.2.8.a.m: According to space [he sets down] ten goblets, made of nyagrodha wood or of rohitaka wood, either with handles or without handles.

12.2.10.a.s: yunajmi te pṛthivīṃ jyotiṣā saheti dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyādhastātpaścādakṣaṃ droṇakalaśaṃ sadaśāpavitram
12.2.10.a.d: युनज्मि ते पृथिवीं ज्योतिषा सहेति दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्याधस्तात्पश्चादक्षं द्रोणकलशं सदशापवित्रम्
12.2.10.a.m: With "I yoke your earth together with light," beneath the southern havirdhāna [cart] behind the axle, [he places] the droṇakalaśa tub together with the fringed strainer.

12.2.11.a.m: Its assignment of wood is identical with that of the vāyavya vessels.

12.2.12.a.s: yunajmi vāyumantarikṣeṇa te sahetyuttarasya havirdhānasyopariṣṭannīḍa ādhavanīyam /
12.2.12.a.d: युनज्मि वायुमन्तरिक्षेण ते सहेत्युत्तरस्य हविर्धानस्योपरिष्टन्नीड आधवनीयम् ।
12.2.12.a.m: With "I yoke your wind together with the intermediate space," upon the northern havirdhāna [cart] inside the cart-bed, [he places] the ādhavanīya jar;

12.2.12.b.s: yunajmi vācaṃ saha sūryeṇa ta iti pradhure pūtabhṛtam
12.2.12.b.d: युनज्मि वाचं सह सूर्येण त इति प्रधुरे पूतभृतम्
12.2.12.b.m: with "I yoke your speech together with the sun," at the front pole-pin, the pūtabhṛt jar.

12.2.13.a.m: Beneath this very havirdhāna [cart] behind the axle, [he places] the three ekadhana pitchers;

12.2.13.b.m: or five, seven, nine, or eleven.

12.2.14.a.m: The pressing-skin on which he measures [the soma] is trimmed to fit the mound, four-folded, with a receptacle on top.

12.2.15.a.s: rakṣohaṇo valagahanaḥ prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavamityadhiṣavaṇacarma prokṣya rakṣoghno valagaghnaḥ prokṣāmi vaiṣṇavāniti grāvṇo rakṣohā tvā valagahā vaiṣṇavamāstṛṇāmītyadhiṣavaṇaphalakayoruttaralomāstīrya rakṣoghno vo valagaghnaḥ saṃsādayāmi vaiṣṇavāniti tasmiṇścaturo grāvṇaḥ prādeśamātrānūrdhvasānūnāhananaprakārānaśmanaḥ saṃsādayati /
12.2.15.a.d: रक्षोहणो वलगहनः प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवमित्यधिषवणचर्म प्रोक्ष्य रक्षोघ्नो वलगघ्नः प्रोक्षामि वैष्णवानिति ग्राव्णो रक्षोहा त्वा वलगहा वैष्णवमास्तृणामीत्यधिषवणफलकयोरुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य रक्षोघ्नो वो वलगघ्नः संसादयामि वैष्णवानिति तस्मिण्श्चतुरो ग्राव्णः प्रादेशमात्रानूर्ध्वसानूनाहननप्रकारानश्मनः संसादयति ।
12.2.15.a.m: Having sprinkled the pressing-skin with "Slaying rakṣases, slaying charms, I sprinkle [the skin] belonging to Viṣṇu," the pressing stones with "Slaying rakṣases, slaying charms, I sprinkle [the stones] belonging to Viṣṇu," and having spread [the skin] with the hair upward on the two pressing boards with "Slaying rakṣases, slaying charms, I spread you belonging to Viṣṇu," he sets down on it four pressing stones measuring a span, high-crested, suitable for pounding, with "Slaying rakṣases, slaying charms, I set you down belonging to Viṣṇu."

12.2.15.b.m: [He sets down] the bottom stone, the widest, in the middle as the fifth.

12.3.2.a.s: apāṃ kṣayā ṛtasya garbhā bhuvanasya gopāḥ śyenā atithayaḥ parvatānāṃ kakubhaḥ prayuto na pātāraḥ /
12.3.2.a.d: अपां क्षया ऋतस्य गर्भा भुवनस्य गोपाः श्येना अतिथयः पर्वतानां ककुभः प्रयुतो न पातारः ।
12.3.2.a.m: "Dwellings of the waters, embryos of cosmic order, protectors of the world, falcons, guests, peaks of the mountains, drinkers not sluggishly;

12.3.2.b.m: invoke Indra with your sound, drive away ailments with your noise;

12.3.2.c.s: yuktā stha vahata svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānamabhivahateti sannānabhimantryāgnīṣomīyavatsavanīyapātrāṇi prayunakti /
12.3.2.c.d: युक्ता स्थ वहत स्वर्गं लोकं यजमानमभिवहतेति सन्नानभिमन्त्र्याग्नीषोमीयवत्सवनीयपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति ।
12.3.2.c.m: you are yoked, carry [the sacrifice], carry the sacrificer to the heavenly world"—having thus addressed [the stones] once set down, he arranges the utensils for the pressing-offering in the manner of the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma.

12.3.2.d.m: He scoops the clarified butter portions in the manner of the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma.

12.3.3.b.m: in the hall with the eastward beam he scoops the clarified butter portions for the animal sacrifice to Agni-Soma;

12.3.3.d.m: on the high altar for the barren cow offering.

12.3.4.a.m: Some say: he scoops the clarified butter portions for the pressing-offering and for the barren cow offering west of the high altar.

12.3.5.a.m: The pieces of wood that he intends to add to the fire on that day, he should sprinkle together with the firewood.

12.3.6.a.m: [The procedure is] identical up to the setting down of the ladles.

12.3.7.a.s: yunajmi tisro vipṛcaḥ sūryasya ta iti srucaḥ sannā abhimantrayate
12.3.7.a.d: युनज्मि तिस्रो विपृचः सूर्यस्य त इति स्रुचः सन्ना अभिमन्त्रयते
12.3.7.a.m: With "I yoke the three separations of your sun," he addresses the ladles once set down.

12.3.8.a.m: Here some prescribe the setting down of the vessels pertaining to Soma.

12.3.9.a.s: āsanyānmā mantrātpāhi kasyāścidabhiśastyā iti purā prātaranuvākājjuhuyāt
12.3.9.a.d: आसन्यान्मा मन्त्रात्पाहि कस्याश्चिदभिशस्त्या इति पुरा प्रातरनुवाकाज्जुहुयात्
12.3.9.a.m: Before the morning recitation, he should make an offering with "Protect me from speech, from the formula, from the accusation of anyone!"

12.3.10.a.m: And [he offers] the Pañcahotṛ formula in the āgnīdhra [shed] for one who desires heaven.

12.3.12.a.m: In the middle of the fire he offers the oblations of clarified butter, the oblations of the animal, and the oblations of sacrificial cake;

12.3.13.a.s: atra rājānamantareṣe grāvasūpāvaharati hṛde tvā soma rājannityetābhyām
12.3.13.a.d: अत्र राजानमन्तरेषे ग्रावसूपावहरति हृदे त्वा सोम राजन्नित्येताभ्याम्
12.3.13.a.m: Here he brings down the king [Soma] into the space between the shafts, onto the pressing stones, with the two formulas: "To the heart you, O king Soma!"

12.3.14.a.s: purā vācaḥ purā vā vayobhyaḥ pravaditoḥ prātaranuvākamupākaroti
12.3.14.a.d: पुरा वाचः पुरा वा वयोभ्यः प्रवदितोः प्रातरनुवाकमुपाकरोति
12.3.14.a.m: Before speech, or before the birds begin to chirp, he introduces the morning recitation.

12.3.15.a.s: prātaryāvabhyo devebhyo 'nubrūhi brahmanvācaṃ yaccha pratiprasthātaḥ savanīyānnirvapa subrahmaṇya subrahmaṇyāmāhvayeti saṃpreṣyati
12.3.15.a.d: प्रातर्यावभ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि ब्रह्मन्वाचं यच्छ प्रतिप्रस्थातः सवनीयान्निर्वप सुब्रह्मण्य सुब्रह्मण्यामाह्वयेति संप्रेष्यति
12.3.15.a.m: He issues the call: "Recite for the gods who travel at dawn! O Brahman, restrain your speech! O pratiprasthātṛ, apportion [the materials for] the pressing-offerings! O Subrahmaṇya, call out the Subrahmaṇyā chant!"

12.3.16.a.m: Some prescribe: "O female Subrahmaṇyā, call out the Subrahmaṇyā chant!"

12.3.17.a.m: With "In my mind I accept your speech," the adhvaryu addresses the hotṛ.

12.3.18.a.s: atra pratiprasthātā savanīyānāṃ pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate
12.3.18.a.d: अत्र प्रतिप्रस्थाता सवनीयानां पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते
12.3.18.a.m: Here the pratiprasthātṛ undertakes the rite of washing his hands and so forth for the pressing-offerings.

12.3.19.a.m: He arranges the utensils according to purpose:

12.4.1.a.m: two potsherds for roasting [and] eight potsherds for the sacrificial cake;

12.4.2.a.m: Some prescribe that at each pressing all [cakes] belong to Indra and are prepared on eleven potsherds.

12.4.4.a.m: In the hall with the eastward beam, the pratiprasthātṛ apportions [the materials for] the pressing-offerings.

12.4.5.a.m: They are all barley, except for those meant for parched grain.

12.4.6.a.s: indrāya harivate dhānā indrāya pūṣaṇvate karambhaṃ sarasvatyai bhāratyai parivāpamindrāya puroḍāśaṃ mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ payasyāmiti
12.4.6.a.d: इन्द्राय हरिवते धाना इन्द्राय पूषण्वते करम्भं सरस्वत्यै भारत्यै परिवापमिन्द्राय पुरोडाशं मित्रावरुणाभ्यां पयस्यामिति
12.4.6.a.m: [He apportions with:] "For Indra with his bay steeds, parched barley; for Indra accompanied by Pūṣan, gruel; for Sarasvatī Bhāratī, parched rice; for Indra, sacrificial cake; for Mitra and Varuṇa, curdled milk."

12.4.7.a.m: When they have been apportioned and poured in together, he undertakes the rite beginning with "This belongs to the gods..."

12.4.8.a.m: At the time of pounding, having set aside those meant for parched grain, he pounds the others.

12.4.9.a.s: kapālānāmupadhānakāle prathamena kapālamantreṇa dhānārthaṃ lājārthaṃ ca kapāle adhiśrayati
12.4.9.a.d: कपालानामुपधानकाले प्रथमेन कपालमन्त्रेण धानार्थं लाजार्थं च कपाले अधिश्रयति
12.4.9.a.m: At the time of setting down the potsherds, he places the potsherd for the parched barley and the potsherd for the parched rice over [the fire] with the first potsherd formula.

12.4.10.a.m: At the time of placing over [the fire], having poured in the husked grains with the formula for placing over [the fire], he prepares the parched barley.

12.4.10.b.m: Having poured in unhusked rice grains, he prepares parched grain.

12.4.11.a.m: Having set on [the fire] the sacrificial cake, he prepares the curd mixture as for an āmikṣā.

12.4.12.a.s: udvāsanakāle dhānā udvāsya vibhāgamantreṇa vibhajyārdhā ājyena saṃyauti /
12.4.12.a.d: उद्वासनकाले धाना उद्वास्य विभागमन्त्रेण विभज्यार्धा आज्येन संयौति ।
12.4.12.a.m: At the time of taking down, having taken down the parched grains and divided them with the division mantra, he mixes half with clarified butter.

12.4.12.b.m: Half he makes into groats according to the procedure for flour.

12.4.14.a.m: With his fingernails, he removes the husks from the parched grains.

12.4.15.a.m: He performs on the fingernails the rules of the mortar and the rules of the pestle.

12.5.1.a.s: yatrābhijānātyabhūduṣā ruśatpaśuriti tatpracarṇyā juhoti śṛṇotvagniḥ samidhā havaṃ ma iti
12.5.1.a.d: यत्राभिजानात्यभूदुषा रुशत्पशुरिति तत्प्रचर्ण्या जुहोति शृणोत्वग्निः समिधा हवं म इति
12.5.1.a.m: When he recognizes [the recitation of the verse]: 'The dawn has appeared, bright with cattle', then with the pracaraṇī spoon he offers [an oblation] with: 'May Agni hear my call with the firewood'.

12.5.2.a.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā saṃpreṣyatyapa iṣya hotarmaitrāvaruṇasya camasādhvaryavādravaikadhanina ādravata neṣṭaḥ patnīmudānayonnetarhotṛcamasena vasatīvarībhiśca cātvālaṃ pratyāsveti
12.5.2.a.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा संप्रेष्यत्यप इष्य होतर्मैत्रावरुणस्य चमसाध्वर्यवाद्रवैकधनिन आद्रवत नेष्टः पत्नीमुदानयोन्नेतर्होतृचमसेन वसतीवरीभिश्च चात्वालं प्रत्यास्वेति
12.5.2.a.m: Having taken another four ladlings, he issues the ritual call: 'Send forth the waters, hotṛ! Camasādhvaryu of the Maitrāvaruṇa, run! Bearers of the Ekadhana waters, run! Neṣṭṛ, bring up the wife! Unnetṛ, come toward the cātvāla with the goblet of the hotṛ and the Vasatīvarī waters!'

12.5.3.a.m: With: 'Come forward, come up', the neṣṭṛ leads up the wife.

12.5.3.c.m: [She is led up] while holding the pot for washing the feet.

12.5.4.a.m: They step forward by the tlrtha path.

12.5.5.a.d: यत्र होतुः प्रातरनुवाकमनुब्रुवत उपशृणुयुस्तदपो ऽध्वर्युर्वन्तीनां गृह्णाति
12.5.5.a.m: Where they hear the hotṛ reciting the morning litany, there the adhvaryu draws from flowing waters.

12.5.6.a.s: yadi na śṛṇoti badhiro ha bhavati vāco ha chidyate
12.5.6.a.d: यदि न शृणोति बधिरो ह भवति वाचो ह छिद्यते
12.5.6.a.m: If he does not hear, he becomes deaf, his speech is cut off.

12.5.7.a.m: If they are far away, he should draw having pushed [the water] toward [himself].

12.5.8.a.m: Having inserted a blade of grass with: 'Divine waters', he makes an offering upon it.

12.5.9.a.m: Or if there was grass beforehand, he should offer upon it.

12.5.10.a.s: kārṣirasīti darbhairāhutimapaplāvya samudrasya vo 'kṣityā unnaya ityabhihutānāṃ maitrāvaruṇacamasena gṛhṇāti
12.5.10.a.d: कार्षिरसीति दर्भैराहुतिमपप्लाव्य समुद्रस्य वो ऽक्षित्या उन्नय इत्यभिहुतानां मैत्रावरुणचमसेन गृह्णाति
12.5.10.a.m: Having made the oblation float away with darbha blades with: 'Thou art Kārṣi', he draws [water] with the goblet of the Maitrāvaruṇa from the waters that have received the offering, with: 'For the imperishableness of the ocean, I draw you up'.

12.5.11.a.m: [The bearers of the Ekadhana waters draw] the Ekadhana waters with: 'I draw thee, the sap of soma from Mount Mūjavat'.

12.5.12.a.s: patnī pannejanīrgṛhṇāti pratyaṅtiṣṭhantī vasubhyo rudrebhya ādityebhya iti
12.5.12.a.d: पत्नी पन्नेजनीर्गृह्णाति प्रत्यङ्तिष्ठन्ती वसुभ्यो रुद्रेभ्य आदित्येभ्य इति
12.5.12.a.m: The wife draws the water for washing the feet, standing facing west, with: 'For the Vasus, for the Rudras, for the Ādityas'.

12.5.13.a.m: With: 'Come forward, come up', the neṣṭṛ leads up the wife.

12.5.14.a.s: apareṇa neṣṭrīyaṃ patnī pannejanīḥ sādayati pratyaṅtiṣṭhantī vasubhyo rudrebhya ādityebhya iti
12.5.14.a.d: अपरेण नेष्ट्रीयं पत्नी पन्नेजनीः सादयति प्रत्यङ्तिष्ठन्ती वसुभ्यो रुद्रेभ्य आदित्येभ्य इति
12.5.14.a.m: Behind the neṣṭṛ's place, the wife sets down the water for washing the feet, standing facing west, with: 'For the Vasus, for the Rudras, for the Ādityas'.

12.5.15.a.m: Just so, she sets them down near the Acchāvāka as he is sitting down.

12.6.1.a.s: hotṛcamasena vasatīvarībhyo niṣicyopari cātvale hotṛcamasaṃ maitrāvaruṇacamasaṃ ca saṃsparśya vasatīvarīrvyānayati
12.6.1.a.d: होतृचमसेन वसतीवरीभ्यो निषिच्योपरि चात्वले होतृचमसं मैत्रावरुणचमसं च संस्पर्श्य वसतीवरीर्व्यानयति
12.6.1.a.m: Having poured out from the Vasatīvarī waters with the goblet of the hotṛ, and having made the goblet of the hotṛ and the goblet of the Maitrāvaruṇa touch each other over the cātvāla, he pours across the Vasatīvarī waters.

12.6.2.a.m:
Recognizing [the verse]: 'The others come together', he pours from the goblet of the hotṛ into the goblet of the Maitrāvaruṇa.

[And] from the goblet of the Maitrāvaruṇa into the goblet of the hotṛ.

12.6.3.a.s: upari cātvāle dhāryamāṇā ubhayīḥ pracaraṇyā samanakti saṃ vo 'naktu varuṇaḥ samindraḥ saṃ pūṣā saṃ dhātā saṃ bṛhaspatiḥ /
12.6.3.a.d: उपरि चात्वाले धार्यमाणा उभयीः प्रचरण्या समनक्ति सं वो ऽनक्तु वरुणः समिन्द्रः सं पूषा सं धाता सं बृहस्पतिः ।
12.6.3.a.m: While they are held over the cātvāla, he anoints both together with the pracaraṇī spoon: 'May Varuṇa anoint you together, may Indra, may Pūṣan, may Dhātṛ, may Bṛhaspati;'

12.6.3.b.s: tvaṣṭā viṣṇuḥ prajayā saṃrārāṇo yajamānāya draviṇaṃ dadhātviti /
12.6.3.b.d: त्वष्टा विष्णुः प्रजया संराराणो यजमानाय द्रविणं दधात्विति ।
12.6.3.b.m: 'May Tvaṣṭṛ, may Viṣṇu, being pleased along with offspring, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer!'

12.6.3.c.m: [And] with: 'As [is fitting], let the yokes be arranged with the yokes'.

12.6.4.a.m: 'Adhvaryu, hast thou approached the waters?' the hotṛ asks the adhvaryu.

12.6.5.a.s: utemanannamuriti pratyuktvā pracaraṇīśeṣātkratukaraṇaṃ juhoti yamagne pṛtsu martyamiti
12.6.5.a.d: उतेमनन्नमुरिति प्रत्युक्त्वा प्रचरणीशेषात्क्रतुकरणं जुहोति यमग्ने पृत्सु मर्त्यमिति
12.6.5.a.m: Having replied: 'And they have bowed down to this one', he offers from the remainder in the pracaraṇī spoon the action-making oblation with: 'That mortal whom thou, O Agni, in the battles...'

12.6.6.a.m: In the absence of that, with four ladlings.

12.6.7.a.m: It is stated that if it is an Agniṣṭoma, he offers.

12.6.8.c.m: If it is an Ukthya, he wipes off [the spoon] upon an enclosing stick;
